f: Greater Tokyo is the most populous metropolitan area in the world.
Kansai International Airport sits on an artificial island in Osaka Bay.
Chubu Centrair airport sits on an artificial island, and Toyota is based nearby.
Fukuoka Airport is one of the closest major airports to its city center.
Sapporo hosted the 1972 Winter Olympics, the first held in Asia.
Naha is the capital of Okinawa, formerly the independent Ryukyu Kingdom.
Hiroshima was the first city hit by an atomic bomb, on August 6, 1945.
Ishigaki is among Japan's southernmost inhabited islands, closer to Taiwan than Tokyo.
Shanghai Maglev train links Pudong airport to the city at about 300 km/h.
Beijing Daxing airport, opened in 2019, has a starfish-shaped terminal.
Guangzhou hosts the Canton Fair, China's largest trade fair.
Shenzhen grew from a fishing town into a megacity after becoming a special economic zone in 1980.
Chengdu is home to the Giant Panda breeding research base.
Chongqing is a municipality built on hills at the meeting of the Yangtze and Jialing rivers.
Hangzhou is the home of Alibaba and the scenic West Lake.
Xi'an is home to the Terracotta Army and was a Silk Road terminus.
Wuhan sits on the Yangtze River and is a major inland rail and river hub.
Nanjing was the capital of China under the Republic of China in the 1920s and 1930s.
Kunming is nicknamed the City of Eternal Spring for its mild climate.
Harbin is famous for its annual International Ice and Snow Festival.
Urumqi is often cited as the city farthest from any ocean in the world.
Lhasa sits near 3,650 m and is the home of the Potala Palace.
Sanya on Hainan island is China's best known tropical beach resort.
Kashgar is an old Silk Road oasis city near the borders of Pakistan and Tajikistan.
Hong Kong International Airport is built on reclaimed land off Lantau Island.
Macao's 2024 gaming revenue of about US$28 billion was over three times that of the Las Vegas Strip (about US$8.8 billion).
Taipei 101 was the world's tallest building from 2004 to 2010.
Kaohsiung is Taiwan's largest port.
Kinmen lies a few kilometers off the coast of Xiamen, mainland China, yet is governed by Taiwan.
The Matsu Islands are administered by Taiwan but lie just off the coast of Fujian.
Incheon airport was named best airport in the world by ACI service quality surveys for 12 straight years, 2005 to 2016.
Busan hosts one of the world's busiest container ports.
Seoul to Jeju is regularly ranked among the busiest air routes in the world.
Pyongyang Metro's Puhung station is dug about 100 m underground, among the deepest metro stations in the world.
Kaesong industrial zone near the DMZ was jointly run with South Korea until 2016.
Changi Airport has an indoor waterfall, the Rain Vortex, in its Jewel complex.
Bangkok's formal ceremonial name is among the longest city names in the world.
Phuket is Thailand's largest island.
Chiang Mai was the capital of the Lanna Kingdom.
Jakarta is sinking quickly and Indonesia is moving its capital to Nusantara in Borneo.
Surabaya is Indonesia's second largest city.
Bali is a Hindu-majority island in a Muslim-majority country.
Medan is the largest city on Sumatra.
Jayapura is the capital of Papua province and near the border with Papua New Guinea.
Banda Aceh was devastated by the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami.
Metro Manila is one of the most densely populated urban areas in the world.
Magellan was killed near Cebu in 1521 at the Battle of Mactan.
Davao City covers about 2,444 sq km, making it the largest city in the Philippines by land area.
Puerto Princesa has a UNESCO-listed underground river.
The Petronas Towers were the world's tallest buildings from 1998 to 2004.
Kota Kinabalu lies below Mount Kinabalu, the highest peak in Borneo.
Kuching is nicknamed Cat City; its name resembles the Malay word for cat, and it has a museum devoted to cats.
Hanoi has been a capital for over a thousand years.
Ho Chi Minh City was formerly known as Saigon.
Da Nang has the Dragon Bridge, which breathes fire on weekend nights.
Phnom Penh sits at the confluence of the Mekong and Tonle Sap rivers.
Siem Reap is the gateway to Angkor Wat, the largest religious monument in the world.
Vientiane is one of the few national capitals on the Mekong River.
Luang Prabang is a UNESCO World Heritage town known for its daily alms-giving ceremony.
Yangon's Shwedagon Pagoda is covered in gold plates.
The government moved from Yangon to Naypyidaw in November 2005; its 20-lane highways are famously empty.
Mandalay was the last royal capital of Burma.
Brunei's Sultan's palace, Istana Nurul Iman, is among the largest residences in the world.
Timor-Leste became independent in 2002, the first new sovereign state of the 21st century.
Sydney Opera House opened in 1973 and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Melbourne-Sydney is one of the busiest domestic air routes in the world.
Brisbane hosts the 2032 Summer Olympics.
Perth is among the most isolated major cities in the world.
Adelaide was founded in 1836 as a free settlement, not a convict colony.
Canberra was purpose-built as the capital and designed by Walter Burley Griffin.
Darwin is the closest Australian capital to Asia and was bombed by Japan in 1942.
Cairns is the gateway to the Great Barrier Reef.
Hobart is the capital of Tasmania, a gateway for Antarctic expeditions.
Alice Springs is about 1,500 km by road from both Darwin and Adelaide.
Uluru is a giant sandstone monolith sacred to the Anangu people.
Broome has dinosaur footprints and a pearling history.
Many residents of Coober Pedy live in underground homes to escape the heat.
Lord Howe Island is a UNESCO World Heritage Site that caps visitors at 400 at a time.
Auckland is built on a volcanic field of about 50 volcanoes.
Wellington is the southernmost national capital in the world.
Christchurch is a main gateway to Antarctica.
Queenstown claims to be the adventure capital of the world.
The Chatham Islands are about 800 km east of mainland New Zealand.
Papua New Guinea has over 800 languages.
Lae is PNG's main port and the start of the Highlands Highway.
Rabaul was buried in ash in 1994 by eruptions of the Tavurvur and Vulcan volcanoes.
Suva hosts the main campus of the University of the South Pacific.
Nadi is Fiji's main international gateway.
Samoa jumped across the International Date Line in 2011, skipping December 30.
Pago Pago has one of the deepest natural harbors in the South Pacific.
Tonga is the Pacific's only monarchy and was a British protected state, not a colony, from 1900 to 1970.
Funafuti's runway doubles as a village green, and Tuvalu's highest point is only 4.6 m above sea level.
Nauru is the world's smallest republic.
Tarawa was the site of a bloody WWII battle in 1943.
Kiritimati, also called Christmas Island, is the world's largest coral atoll and among the first places to see a new day.
The Marshall Islands were the site of US nuclear tests at Bikini and Enewetak.
Kwajalein is the world's largest atoll by enclosed lagoon area and hosts a US Army missile test range.
Pohnpei is the site of the ancient stone city of Nan Madol.
Chuuk Lagoon holds a large wreck fleet from Operation Hailstone in 1944.
Palau's Rock Islands and Jellyfish Lake are major diving attractions.
Guam is a US territory and hosts major US military bases.
Saipan was the site of a major WWII battle in 1944.
Honiara is built on Guadalcanal, site of a major WWII campaign.
Vanuatu's Mount Yasur volcano has erupted almost continuously for centuries.
New Caledonia holds a large share of the world's nickel reserves.
Papeete is on Tahiti, and French Polynesia includes Bora Bora.
Rarotonga is encircled by a single 32 km road.
Niue is a raised coral island, among the world's largest, and self-governs in free association with New Zealand.
Wallis and Futuna is a French overseas collectivity.
Pitcairn was settled by the Bounty mutineers in 1790.
Many Norfolk Islanders descend from the Bounty mutineers.
The 1942 Battle of Midway was a turning point of the Pacific War.
Wake Island was captured by Japan in December 1941 after a US garrison defended it.
Airbus opened its first A320 final assembly line outside Europe next to Tianjin airport in 2008.
On August 12 2021 all Qingdao flights moved overnight from Liuting to the new Jiaodong airport.
Xiamen became one of China's first four special economic zones in 1980.
Zhengzhou set up the first futures exchange approved by China's State Council in October 1990.
Changsha's airport maglev, opened May 6 2016, runs 18.5 km to Changsha South station in about 10 minutes.
The 1931 Mukden Incident, which led to Japan's occupation of Manchuria, began in Shenyang.
Dalian began in 1898 as Dalny, a commercial port founded by Russia. It took its present name in 1981.
Ningbo-Zhoushan is the world's busiest port by cargo tonnage, at 1.22 billion tons in 2021.
Fuzhou is nicknamed the Banyan City because of the banyan trees that line its streets.
The March 11 2011 tsunami flooded Sendai Airport up to the terminal's second floor. It reopened April 13 2011.
Daegu Airport is shared with the 11th Fighter Wing of the Korean air force, so photographing the apron is banned.
Sakurajima, an active volcano across the bay, regularly dusts Kagoshima with volcanic ash.
TSMC's first chip plant in Japan, in Kikuyo near Kumamoto, held its opening ceremony in February 2024.
Miyazaki is a popular spring training base for Japanese pro baseball teams, including the Yomiuri Giants.
During Japan's isolation era, Dejima in Nagasaki was the only port open to Dutch traders.
Kobe Airport, opened in 2006, sits on a man-made island in Osaka Bay south of Port Island.
Matsuyama's Dogo Onsen is often called Japan's oldest hot spring; its main bathhouse dates to 1894.
Neighboring Beppu has more than 2,000 hot spring sources, among the most of any resort in the world.
Hakodate was one of the first Japanese ports opened to foreign trade under the 1854 Convention of Kanagawa.
Takamatsu is the ferry gateway to Naoshima, the Seto Inland Sea island known for its art museums.
Kochi Ryoma Airport is named after Sakamoto Ryoma, the local samurai who helped topple the shogunate.
Kanazawa's Kenroku-en is one of Japan's three great gardens; its airport, Komatsu, is shared with the air force.
The Jikji, the oldest surviving book printed with movable metal type, was printed in Cheongju in 1377.
Gwangju was the site of the May 1980 pro-democracy uprising, commemorated every year on May 18.
Ulsan hosts Hyundai's main car plant, one of the largest single automobile factories in the world.
Yeosu hosted the 2012 World Expo, themed on the living ocean and coast.
Pohang is home to the headquarters and main steelworks of POSCO, one of the largest steelmakers in the world.
Bubble tea was popularized in Taichung in the 1980s; the Chun Shui Tang teahouse claims to have invented it.
Magong is the main town of the Penghu archipelago, about 90 islands in the middle of the Taiwan Strait.
Tainan was Taiwan's capital for over 200 years and the site of the Dutch Fort Zeelandia, begun in 1624.
Taitung is the gateway to Orchid Island and Green Island, both served by small planes from its airport.
Haikou is the capital of Hainan, which China is developing as a free trade port with duty-free shopping.
Guiyang has become a big data hub, hosting the data centers that run Apple's iCloud service in China.
Jinan is known as the City of Springs, with Baotu Spring the most famous of its 72 named springs.
Changchun was the capital of Japanese-controlled Manchukuo from 1932 to 1945, under the name Hsinking.
Lanzhou beef noodle soup, now sold across China, originated in the city; its airport is about 70 km away.
Taiyuan is the capital of Shanxi, one of the largest coal-producing provinces in China.
Nanning has hosted the China-ASEAN Expo every year since 2004.
Zhuhai hosts the biennial China airshow and is the mainland end of the 55 km bridge to Hong Kong and Macau.
Wenzhou is known for its private entrepreneurs and a large diaspora in Europe, especially Italy and France.
Hohhot, capital of Inner Mongolia, is home to the dairy giants Yili and Mengniu.
Hefei is home to EV maker NIO's main factories and the University of Science and Technology of China.
Shijiazhuang grew from a village into a provincial capital after two railway lines crossed there in the early 1900s.
The Nanchang Uprising of August 1 1927 is commemorated as the founding of China's People's Liberation Army.
Wuxi sits on Lake Tai, China's third largest freshwater lake, and its airport is shared with Suzhou.
Shantou was one of China's first four special economic zones in 1980; its airport is in neighboring Jieyang.
Yinchuan, capital of Ningxia, lies near the Western Xia imperial tombs, nicknamed China's pyramids.
Quanzhou was the Zayton of Marco Polo's travels and became a UNESCO World Heritage site in 2021.
Lijiang's old town, a UNESCO site since 1997, is the heartland of the Naxi people.
Yantai is home to Changyu, founded in 1892 and China's oldest winery.
Xining is the starting point of the Qinghai-Tibet Railway, which climbs above 5,000 m on its way to Lhasa.
Guilin's karst peaks along the Li River appear on the back of China's 20 yuan banknote.
